question: Does any near-duplicate image pair cross a partition boundary under different patient ids (leakage), and how many retained images are near-duplicate views of another image of the same patient (effective sample size)?

method.note: dHash is a screen, not a proof: a flagged pair may be two different images sharing coarse gradient structure. Every flagged pair is re-checked for pixel identity and both verdicts are reported, so exact and approximate matches are never conflated. A zero in leakage_cross_partition_different_patient is the result this module exists to establish; it is not evidence of absence for relationships dHash cannot see (heavy crops, large rotations).

leakage.interpretation: cross_partition_different_patient > 0 would mean the same photograph reached two partitions under two patient ids, which patient-level splitting cannot prevent. cross_partition_same_patient > 0 would mean the patient-level invariant itself is broken.

label_contradictions.interpretation: A near-duplicate pair whose binary labels disagree is irreducible label noise: identical or near-identical inputs with opposite targets. Only pairs where BOTH members carry a lesion polygon reach the primary A_lesion_polygon condition; the rest are filtered out of it.

effective_sample_size.redundant_member_selection: WARNING, read before quoting redundant_by_binary_class: the member counted as redundant is sorted(cluster)[1:], i.e. chosen by image_id alphabetical order, NOT by any property of the image. Because a contradictory cluster is typically ('normal/...', 'opmd/...') and 'normal' sorts first, the opmd copy is mechanically the one counted. So the positive/negative split of redundant images is an artifact of that ordering and must NOT be read as 'this many positives are duplicates'. The defensible figures are n_clusters_above_one and n_distinct_after_collapse. A cluster whose two members carry different binary labels cannot be collapsed at all without choosing a label, which is why those are reported separately under label_contradictions.
effective_sample_size.interpretation: Clusters are connected components over same-patient near-duplicate pairs. n_redundant_images counts cluster members beyond the first, i.e. how many retained rows carry no new image content. This is an upper bound on redundancy at this threshold, not a correction to any recorded count.

verdict.reading: Reported at the threshold fixed before the scan, not at a threshold chosen afterwards. At max_hamming=6 the scan flags pairs that cross a partition under different patient ids, and the honest conclusion is still that there is no leakage -- established by three facts recorded above rather than by lowering the threshold: (1) NONE of the flagged pairs is pixel-identical, (2) all of them are negative-negative, with no positive and no member of the A_lesion_polygon condition involved, and (3) the Hamming histogram is empty at 1-3, so no flagged pair can be a re-encoding of another. The flagged pairs are the left tail of the background distribution: intra-oral photographs of different patients taken on the same rig with the same framing share coarse gradient structure. The threshold is left at 6 on the record; it was a loose choice and the artifact says so rather than being re-run at 3.
verdict.patient_level_invariant: cross_partition_same_patient == 0 confirms the split's own invariant independently of the split code that asserts it.

hamming_distribution.what_it_shows: The distribution is bimodal with a hard gap: every pixel-identical duplicate sits at Hamming 0 and bins 1-3 are EMPTY, while bins 4 upward rise smoothly into the background mode near 31. A re-encoded, rescaled or brightness-shifted copy of a photograph lands at Hamming 1-3, so the empty gap is positive evidence that this dataset contains no approximate duplicates -- not merely that none were found. It also shows the pre-registered threshold of 6 was too loose: the pairs it adds above zero are the left tail of the background, which is why none of them is pixel-identical.

test_partition_note: The test partition's membership is read to label pairs, but no test metric is computed and no model is fitted anywhere in this module.
